newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek bourse corrects, seen rebounding next week.
newsitem.headline: Greek bourse corrects, seen rebounding next week.

text.p: Greek stocks closed down 0.43 percent on Friday on high volume after a bout of profit taking with fund managers attributing the correction to cross-sectoral portfolio reallocations and expecting a rebound next week.

"The market corrected on Friday after profit taking. Orders are cyclical, moving from one sector to the other. On Friday, we moved from banks to construction shares," said Mihalis Eleftheriou, a fund manager at Alpha Mutual Funds.
Banks are a good sector to invest in because of recent news of mergers and privatisations. They are considered a solid and stable market performer, Eleftheriou said.
Block trades in shares of Alpha Credit, Aluminium of Greece, Michaniki, Alte and Aspis Pronoia boosted trading volume.
The Athens general share index closed 0.43 percent or 5.07 points down at 1166.19 from Thursday's 1171.26, after opening at 1173.48.

Construction shares led after climbing 3.82, with leasing shares following with a rise of 3.45. Insurance ended 0.22 percent up while industrials lost 0.74 percent, banks slipped 0.31 percent and investment shares ended 0.82 percent up.
Friday's turnover was 17.3 billion drachmas on volume of 5.8 million shares. Gainers led losers 139 to 86 with 24 issues unchanged on 249 traded.
